cohort: 40 patients aged 18-60 years, classified as American Society of Anesthesiologist (ASA) I or II, who were scheduled for lower segment cesarean section and candidates for subarachnoid block.
finding: Low-dose intravenous ketamine (0.2mg/kg) significantly reduced the incidence of post-spinal shivering (25%) compared to tramadol (0.5mg/kg) (55%), with a lower incidence of intraoperative side effects.
mod_finding: Low-dose intravenous ketamine is more effective than tramadol in reducing post-spinal shivering during lower segment cesarean section.
